title: History of Philosophy Colloquium: Meaning: the final frontier
speaker: Ian James (University of Cambridge)
description: History of Philosophy Research Colloquium. Recent work in the life sciences increasingly recognises meaning, purposiveness and interpretation at every level of biological organisation. The talk argues that this poses a problem for the language of biological theory: the literal, descriptive terms used for observable morphologies and genetic sequences pull against the figural, metaphorical terms needed for meaning. The language of mechanism, and attempts to keep or move beyond it, is where this tension plays out. Followed by drinks at Café Hofman; everyone is welcome.
